title: Win Probability, Ball by Ball: Building a Model for Sunrisers Hyderabad
dek: How likely is Sunrisers Hyderabad to win from here? A transparent win-probability model, fitted on every other IPL chase, answers the question halfway through any run chase.
excerpt: Fitted on the rest of the league's chases, a simple halfway model expected Sunrisers Hyderabad to win a certain number of their chases; they won fewer. The model is small enough to explain in a single table.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: Fitted on {{ev:wp-n}} chases by other sides, the model gives a chasing side {{ev:wp-easy}} needing under eight an over with no more than one wicket down, and {{ev:wp-hard}} needing twelve or more with four or more down.
From the positions SRH reached in {{ev:wp-m}} chases, the model expected {{ev:wp-exp}} wins; they won {{ev:wp-act}}.
The whole model fits in one table: required rate by wickets lost.

sections.heading: A Model You Can Read
body: Win-probability models usually hide inside software. This one is deliberately simple: take every IPL chase by sides other than SRH, note the required rate and wickets lost after ten overs, and record how often the chasing side won.

Fitted on {{ev:wp-n}} chases, the model gives a chasing side {{ev:wp-easy}} needing under eight an over with no more than one wicket down, and {{ev:wp-hard}} needing twelve or more with four or more down.

sections.heading: SRH Against the Model
body: Sunrisers Hyderabad reached the eleventh over in {{ev:wp-m}} chases. From those positions the model expected {{ev:wp-exp}} wins; they won {{ev:wp-act}}.
They have finished chases worse than the positions suggested.

sections.heading: Ball by Ball
body: The same table can be built for every over, which is how broadcast win-probability graphics work. CricField uses the halfway point here because it has the most data per cell.

sections.heading: What the Model Ignores
body: It ignores venue, the batters at the crease and the bowlers still to bowl. Adding those would sharpen it, at the cost of transparency and larger data needs per cell.
Rain-shortened chases are treated as full twenty-over chases, so a few positions are misclassified.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Start Simple
body: A two-variable table already explains much of who wins a chase. Sunrisers Hyderabad have fallen short of it.
Extensions should be judged by how much they improve on this baseline.

seo.metaTitle: Win probability: a transparent model for SRH chases
seo.metaDescription: A one-table win-probability model fitted on every IPL chase, and how Sunrisers Hyderabad have performed against it.

methodology: Built from the CricField warehouse (Cricsheet ball-by-ball data, regulation innings). Models are fitted on the warehouse itself and described in full here. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Cells with fewer than ten chases fall back to the overall chase win rate. SRH chases are excluded when fitting.
